card.statement:
In [10] the authors also describe the cohomology of (co)stalks of the intersection cohomology complex on two different relative compactifications of the stack of torsors on $C$ for a parabolic subgroup of $G$. We expect that as above this description remains valid for any field of good characteristic, and that this statement can be obtained by a variation of the techniques used in the present paper. This will be the subject of future work.

1.2. Relation with semiinfinite sheaves

The way we approach this question is inspired by results of Gaitsgory from [17], but used “in the reverse direction.” Namely, consider the affine Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}$ of $G$, an ind-projective ind-scheme over $\mathbb{F}$. Let $T\subset B$ be a maximal torus, and denote by $U$ the unipotent radical of $B$. We call “semiinfinite Iwahori subgroup” the group ind-scheme

$\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}:=\mathcal{L}^{+}T\ltimes\mathcal{L}U,$

where $\mathcal{L}^{+}(-)$, resp.  $\mathcal{L}(-)$, denotes the arc space, resp. loop space, associated with a scheme over $\mathbb{F}$. This group acts on $\mathrm{Gr}$ on the left, and following Gaitsgory one can make sense of the $\infty$ -category $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})$ of $\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}$ -equivariant sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}$. More specifically the construction of this $\infty$ -category requires a choice of coefficient field $\Bbbk$;11 1

In case $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}$, one can work with sheaves for the analytic topology, and $\Bbbk$ can be arbitrary. For a general field $\mathbb{F}$ we work with étale sheaves, and have to impose the usual restrictions on $\Bbbk$ in this setting. See §3.4 for details. Gaitsgory has explicitly studied the case when $\Bbbk$ has characteristic $0$, but as we have explained in [2] the definition makes sense for any $\Bbbk$, and most of its formal properties are insensitive to this choice. Objects of this $\infty$ -category are called semiinfinite sheaves.

The $\infty$ -category $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})$ admits a natural t-structure called the perverse t-structure, whose heart $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})^{\heartsuit}$ contains a remarkable object which Gaitsgory calls the semi-infinite intersection cohomology sheaf, and that we prefer calling the Gaitsgory sheaf. This object is denoted $\mathrm{Ga}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}$ here. (In particular, the simple objects in the abelian category $\mathsf{Shv}(\mathrm{I}^{{\frac{\infty}{2}}}\backslash\mathrm{Gr})^{\heartsuit}$ are naturally parametrized by the coweight lattice $\mathbf{Y}=X_{*}(T)$; its seems natural to call these objects intersection cohomology complexes, but $\mathrm{Ga}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}$ is not one of them, in fact this object has infinite length.)

One of the main results of [2] is the computation of the dimension of the cohomology of stalks and costalks of $\mathrm{Ga}^{\frac{\infty}{2}}$ in the case when $\Bbbk$ has good characteristic, generalizing the description in the case when $\mathrm{char}(\Bbbk)=0$ given by Gaitsgory in [17]. Here also the answer naturally involves the $q$ -analogue of Kostant’s partition function. But, while Gaitsgory’s proof uses the known description of the stalks of $\mathrm{IC}_{\overline{\mathrm{Bun}}_{B}}$ (in the case he considers) from [10], ours is intrinsic to the setting of (constructible) sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}$, and is used in the present paper as the main input to obtain our version of the results of [10] for general fields.

paper.title: Modular intersection cohomology of Drinfeld's compactifications
paper.abstract: We compute the dimension of the cohomology of stalks of intersection cohomology complexes on Zastava schemes and Drinfeld compactifications associated with a connected reductive algebraic group $G$, in case the characteristic of the coefficients field $\Bbbk$ is good for $G$. In particular, we show that these dimensions do not depend on the choice of $\Bbbk$.
